Production Planner

Technical Requirements Document

Build a public daily production planner for a fictional juice supplier. The system turns three fixed recipes, resource limits, and order bounds into an optimal production recommendation, then lets a reviewer save and compare scenarios in the same browser.

# 2 Executive technical summary

Use a Next.js frontend and a separate FastAPI backend in one public GitHub repository. The browser calls the Python API directly. SciPy linprog with method="highs" solves the continuous linear program. Named scenarios remain in localStorage; there is no backend database, sign-in, or cross-device synchronization.

Both applications initially target separate Vercel Hobby projects. Week one includes a deployment investigation capped at 10 hours. Packaging SciPy and meeting the five-second end-to-end target after inactivity are unverified. That investigation must pass before this hosting choice is treated as proven. A failure requires evidence and a new owner decision, not an automatic paid upgrade or a weaker performance target.

This is an approved build specification, not a claim that the application exists or its release checks have passed. The fictional sample model was solved locally during planning; its expected values appear in Section 20.

# 3 Source and scope

The attached PRD is authoritative. Its printed status says "First draft for review," but Allen explicitly instructed that it be treated as the approved scope. All FR01–FR14 and NFR01–NFR09 remain applicable. Technical interview decisions resolve the PRD items delegated to this document.

The MVP plans one day for orange–apple, apple–pineapple, and tropical juice. It has three ingredients, one shared processing resource, fractional litres, no waste, and constant contribution and processing time per litre. Recipes are editable between calculations and fixed within each calculation. Contribution is entered directly in AUD per litre, and minimum orders may force negative total contribution.

Excluded: accounts, cloud scenario storage, collaboration, arbitrary products or resources, multi-day inventory, integer bottles, purchasing, uncertainty, recipe optimization, exports, Docker, and commercial forecasting. No uptime percentage or commercial throughput commitment is defined. Free services only is a confirmed constraint.

# 6 Technical capabilities

The frontend owns form text, field errors, pending state, result presentation, input revision tracking, named scenario management and comparison. It never constructs a second independent optimization model. The backend owns trusted input validation, exact minimum-order checks, matrix construction, solver execution, post-solve validation and the response contract.

Persistence is one versioned browser collection. Writes are explicit and coordinated between tabs. Infrastructure consists of the two Vercel projects, HTTPS, CORS, one API firewall rule, and GitHub Actions. There are no queues, background jobs, accounts, database migrations or application cache. Calculation responses use Cache-Control: no-store; stored results are user-managed records, not a shared server cache.

# 7 Architecture

![The Next.js frontend reads and writes browser storage and calls a separate public FastAPI service over HTTPS. FastAPI validates inputs and calls SciPy HiGHS. GitHub Actions checks both repository folders and Allen releases two projects manually.](data:image/png;base64,)

Figure 1 Application boundaries and data flow

## Calculation flow

1. Read and validate the current form. Capture an immutable canonical input snapshot and an input revision. Disable duplicate Calculate clicks while that request is active; editing remains enabled.
2. POST the snapshot to the backend. Validate it independently, including fixed identifiers, decimal precision, recipe totals, bounds and body size. Compute every minimum-order shortage using exact entered decimals.
3. If no shortage exists, minimize the negative contribution vector with linprog. Accept only solver status zero with a finite solution that passes the resource and order checks. Recompute contribution and resource totals from the returned quantities.
4. On return, verify the API/model versions, response shape, active request identity and input revision. Apply results only when all match. Render tables and charts from the same response. Discard an earlier response after an edit, load or replacement request.

Vercel supports FastAPI as a Python Function with a supported entrypoint \[S04, S05\]. This platform capability does not establish that the selected SciPy bundle or latency target has passed the project spike.

# 9 Data design

## Planning inputs and exact validation

PlanningInputs is the shared calculation and saved-input schema. The API transports user-entered decimal fields as strings. The frontend trims input and rejects excess decimal places before canonicalizing equivalent valid decimals. Backend Decimal parsing verifies precision and ranges independently; floats are introduced only for solver matrices. Canonicalization never rounds an invalid entry into a valid one.

| **Field**                    | **Type and unit**              | **Required constraints**                                                                                                                |
| ---------------------------- | ------------------------------ | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| blends                       | Array of exactly 3 records     | Exactly one of orange_apple, apple_pineapple and tropical; no duplicates or additional products                                         |
| recipe_percent               | Object of 3 decimal strings, % | Each 0–100; at most 2 decimal places; exact total 100.00. Convert to integer basis points totaling 10000.                               |
| Excluded recipe ingredients  | Fixed decimal zero             | orange_apple pineapple=0; apple_pineapple orange=0. Tropical allows all three. Zero shares are permitted by the approved numeric rules. |
| profit_aud_per_litre         | Decimal string, AUD/L          | Required; −1000 to 1000; at most 2 decimal places                                                                                       |
| processing_minutes_per_litre | Decimal string, min/L          | Required; 0–60; at most 3 decimal places                                                                                                |
| min_litres                   | Decimal string, L              | Default 0; 0–10000; at most 3 decimal places                                                                                            |
| max_litres                   | Decimal string, L              | Required; 0–10000; at most 3 decimal places; minimum ≤ maximum                                                                          |
| available_ingredient_litres  | 3 named decimal strings, L     | orange apple pineapple each required; 0–10000; at most 3 decimal places                                                                 |
| processing_capacity_hours    | Decimal string, hours          | Required; 0–24; at most 3 decimal places; multiply exactly by 60 to get minutes                                                         |

PlanningInputs contains user model values only. API and model versions belong to the request envelope and stored result metadata, not the editable input snapshot. Recalculation uses the current application version constants while preserving saved user values; an older result remains outdated until the current model solves those inputs successfully.

Accept plain signed decimal syntax with a leading digit and optional fractional digits. Reject negative values in fields required to be nonnegative; negative zero canonicalizes to zero. Reject empty input, booleans, JSON numeric substitutes, exponent notation, comma-formatted numbers, NaN, Infinity, unknown fields and unsupported identifiers. Leading or trailing UI whitespace is trimmed before submission. A field such as 1.0000 is rejected where only three decimal places are allowed, even though its value is numerically equivalent.

## Calculation records

An optimal result contains finite unrounded quantities, total contribution, resource totals, utilization and binding flags, plus the request ID, API/model versions and solver metadata. An infeasible result contains every positive minimum-order shortage and no production recommendation or contribution figure. An error is not a calculation result. Section 10 defines the field contract.

## Saved collection dictionary

| **Record and field**         | **Type and rule**                                                                                                                            |
| ---------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| ScenarioStore.schema_version | Integer 1. Unsupported versions are preserved and block mutation until a supported reader or explicit reset is chosen.                       |
| ScenarioStore.revision       | Nonnegative integer, incremented once per successful collection mutation. Used with an exclusive browser write lock.                         |
| ScenarioStore.scenarios      | Array with at most 20 entries. Preserved unreadable entries count toward capacity; there is no silent eviction.                              |
| SavedScenario.id             | UUID string, generated on creation and stable through rename/update                                                                          |
| SavedScenario.name           | Trimmed string of 1–50 characters. Unique after trim and case normalization. Render as text, never HTML.                                     |
| created_at and updated_at    | UTC ISO 8601 strings. Creation remains unchanged; each explicit successful mutation updates updated_at. Display in the visitor's local time. |
| inputs                       | Required valid PlanningInputs. Invalid incomplete forms cannot be saved as a draft.                                                          |
| result                       | OptimalResult, InfeasibleResult or null. Valid inputs may be saved before calculation or after infeasibility.                                |
| result_input_snapshot        | PlanningInputs or null. Immutable snapshot for the stored result; canonical comparison checks correspondence.                                |
| result_outdated              | Boolean. True after any model input edit until successful calculation for that revision. Rename alone does not alter it.                     |
| Transient planner state      | In-memory form text, field errors, request identity, input revision and unsaved flag. No automatic persistence is promised.                  |

![ScenarioStore contains zero to twenty SavedScenario records. Each scenario has exactly one PlanningInputs record and zero or one stored calculation. A calculation includes a snapshot that must match those inputs and the current model version.](data:image/png;base64,)

Figure 2 Browser collection records and result correspondence

## Storage lifecycle and concurrency

Store one JSON envelope at localStorage key production-planner:scenarios:v1. There are no database tables, indexes, server-side ownership records or audit history. Browser origin is the persistence boundary. Preview origins have separate collections from production; clearing browser data can remove saved work. Do not present localStorage as backup or encrypted storage.

Every create, rename, update, delete and reset acquires the same exclusive Web Lock, rereads the latest stored envelope, and compares its revision with the revision loaded by that tab. A mismatch stops the write and offers reload of the saved collection while preserving the current planner inputs. The storage event marks other tabs as needing a reload. Web Locks coordinates same-origin tabs \[S13\]; localStorage alone is not a compare-and-swap mechanism.

![The planner requests a browser write lock. While holding it, it rereads localStorage and checks the collection revision. A changed revision stops the save and requires reload. Otherwise it validates and writes one new collection revision, releases the lock and reports success only after the write succeeds.](data:image/png;base64,)

Figure 3 An explicit save with concurrency protection

Validate name uniqueness and capacity against the latest collection inside the lock. Write the complete new envelope once; acknowledge success only if setItem succeeds. Update/delete an existing record is allowed at capacity. Save as new requires a free slot and distinct name. Unsupported locking capability disables persistent mutation with a clear message while calculation remains usable; verify lock support in the chosen browser matrix.

If the envelope parses but some entries fail validation, load the valid entries and preserve invalid raw records unchanged. Warn and allow only explicit confirmed removal of an unreadable entry. If the envelope cannot be parsed, or its format is unsupported, preserve the original bytes and block writes that would overwrite them. A confirmed collection reset is the recovery of last resort. No automatic corruption repair, format downgrade, or data eviction is permitted.

Reopening a saved scenario loads its inputs and any compatible current result immediately. Warn before replacing unsaved current work with another scenario. Input edits never update the stored entry automatically. Comparison requires two distinct saved entries, both optimal, current and matching the current model version and their stored inputs. Compute each difference as scenario B minus scenario A using unrounded numbers.

# 10 API contracts

Base URLs come from environment configuration. The API is anonymous and stateless. It neither receives scenario names nor creates saved scenarios. GET /health reports build/API/model identity and service readiness without running optimization; it is not proof of full solver health.

| **Method and path**   | **Success**                                               | **Errors and purpose**                                                                                         |
| --------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| POST /api/v1/optimize | 200 with status optimal or infeasible                     | Validate and calculate one fixed model. Never return a timed-out incumbent as optimal.                         |
| GET /health           | 200: status, api_version, model_version, build identifier | Configuration failure must fail deployment readiness; omit secret values from response.                        |
| OPTIONS on API routes | CORS preflight response                                   | Allow the paired frontend, POST/GET as needed and Content-Type. No credentials or browser-held backend secret. |

## Optimize request

Content-Type must be application/json. The body is at most 16384 bytes, including whitespace. Bound streamed reads as well as Content-Length; do not trust the header alone. Reject unsupported content encoding rather than decompressing an unbounded request. JSON syntax and the schema are validated before the solver is called. The request shape below is normative; Section 20 contains the complete sample.

| **Request field**           | **Contract**                                                                                                               |
| --------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| api_version                 | Integer 1                                                                                                                  |
| model_version               | String juice-day-v1                                                                                                        |
| blends\[\]                  | id; recipe_percent with orange/apple/pineapple; profit_aud_per_litre; processing_minutes_per_litre; min_litres; max_litres |
| available_ingredient_litres | Object with exactly orange, apple and pineapple decimal-string fields                                                      |
| processing_capacity_hours   | Decimal string in the approved hours range                                                                                 |

## Optimal response

| **Response field**                   | **Type and meaning**                                                                                                                    |
| ------------------------------------ | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| api_version model_version request_id | Integer, string and server-generated UUID; required on application responses                                                            |
| status                               | Literal optimal                                                                                                                         |
| production_litres                    | Object with the three fixed blend IDs and finite unrounded numbers                                                                      |
| profit_contribution_aud              | Finite number recomputed from unrounded production and contribution coefficients                                                        |
| resources\[\]                        | Exactly orange/apple/pineapple/processing. Each record has id, unit, available, used, remaining, utilization_percent and is_fully_used. |
| Resource units                       | Ingredient records use litres; processing uses minutes. remaining = available − used before display normalization.                      |
| utilization_percent                  | Finite number for positive capacity; null for zero capacity. Display zero capacity as No capacity, not 0% or 100%.                      |
| reached_demand_caps                  | Array of blend IDs whose quantity is within the litre tolerance of its maximum                                                          |
| numerical_residuals                  | Array of accepted tiny bound/resource residuals, empty when none. Each entry identifies the constraint, residual and unit.              |
| solver                               | method=highs, status=0, duration_ms finite and nonnegative                                                                              |
| duration_ms                          | Backend processing duration; does not replace the browser click-to-render measurement or include all platform startup time              |

Only return this shape when linprog reports optimal success, all output values are finite, and the independent plan checks pass. Recompute usage, remaining values and contribution from quantities rather than trusting unrelated solver fields. Validate the response on the frontend as well; unknown status or incompatible version is a calculation failure.

## Infeasible response

Return HTTP 200 with status=infeasible, the common versions/request ID, and shortages\[\]. Each shortage record contains resource_id, unit, required, available and shortfall, all finite numbers with positive shortfall. Include every violated resource. Omit production_litres and profit_contribution_aud. The check uses exact decimal minimum usage before conversion to solver floats; a genuinely positive tiny shortage must not be hidden by three-decimal display rounding.

With nonnegative coefficients and validated minimum ≤ maximum bounds, the minimum vector is feasible whenever its resource usage fits. Therefore a later solver infeasible status after the exact precheck is an unexpected solver/numerical failure, not an invented shortage explanation. Treat solver unbounded status as an implementation error because finite upper bounds are mandatory.

## Application error envelope

Application errors return error.code, a safe error.message, request_id, and optional error.fields containing path and message. Validation details omit raw input values and stack traces. Frontend field paths map to the fixed form fields. Firewall and hosting responses may be HTML or lack readable CORS headers; the frontend must also handle an unreadable/non-JSON response safely.

| **HTTP** | **Application code or source**      | **User behaviour**                                                                                                     |
| -------- | ----------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| 400      | INVALID_JSON                        | Explain that the request could not be read; preserve inputs.                                                           |
| 413      | PAYLOAD_TOO_LARGE                   | Request exceeds 16 KiB; no solver call.                                                                                |
| 415      | UNSUPPORTED_MEDIA_TYPE              | Require JSON with supported encoding; no solver call.                                                                  |
| 422      | VALIDATION_ERROR                    | Show all available field errors; correct values before retry.                                                          |
| 409      | MODEL_VERSION_MISMATCH              | Ask to refresh for the current application version; preserve saved data.                                               |
| 429      | Vercel firewall rate limit          | If readable, show a temporary limit message and manual retry later; otherwise use the network/service failure message. |
| 503      | CALCULATION_TIMEOUT                 | Solver reached its one-second limit; no optimal result.                                                                |
| 500      | CALCULATION_ERROR or INTERNAL_ERROR | Nonoptimal/numerical/invalid output or unexpected exception; no traceback to visitor.                                  |
| —        | Browser timeout or network failure  | Stop waiting at ten seconds; preserve inputs and allow manual Retry.                                                   |

Repeated optimize calls have no storage side effects. No idempotency key is required, and equal inputs may yield different equally optimal plans. Pagination and CRUD endpoints are inapplicable because named-scenario operations happen locally. A browser abort does not guarantee termination of a running server calculation; the solver limit still applies.

# 11 Security and privacy

All public visitors have the same calculation capability. Authentication, authorization roles, sessions, user tokens and tenancy are inapplicable to this anonymous demo. CORS restricts browser cross-origin access; it is not authentication and does not stop command-line clients. Do not embed an API secret in the frontend to simulate protection. Use HTTPS for hosted frontend and backend.

Enforce the fixed schema, numeric bounds, exact recipe rules, 16 KiB actual-body limit and one-second solver limit on the backend. Configure one Vercel WAF fixed-window rule for POST /api/v1/optimize, keyed by IP, at 30 requests per 60 seconds. Exclude OPTIONS so preflight does not consume calculation allowance. Hobby currently includes one rate-limit rule; counters are regional and shared networks can trigger the same IP limit \[S07\]. This is modest abuse control, not a global traffic guarantee.

Use exact production/preview origin allowlists and allow_credentials=false. Pair each public frontend preview with a backend preview; do not allow arbitrary subdomains. Disable deployment authentication only as approved for the demo/preview projects. Vercel supports this project-level setting on Hobby \[S09\]. Apply the same input safeguards to preview URLs; public preview access is not private access.

The API processes recipe, resource and contribution values transiently. Application code must not persist requests, scenario data or result bodies. Application logs contain request ID, status/error category and duration only. Configure access/error middleware to avoid echoed validation bodies. Vercel may independently collect request metadata such as IP and path; do not claim the provider stores nothing. Explain this distinction and browser-local saving in the README and dashboard help.

Render user names through normal React text escaping. Avoid dangerouslySetInnerHTML and unnecessary third-party scripts. Keep CLI credentials in the owner's credential store and any future automation credentials in GitHub Secrets. Exclude local env files and credentials from Git; scan the repository before publication. Review locked dependency licences and vulnerabilities before release; no unsupported legal/compliance certification is claimed.

# 12 Reliability and error handling

## Request freshness and result states

Use an increasing in-memory input revision and a unique active request identity. Every model edit or scenario load increments the revision, flags any existing result outdated, and aborts the old browser request when practical. A new request captures both values and a deep canonical snapshot. A returned response is applied only when the active identity and current revision still match, even if edited inputs were later changed back to their original values.

Disable duplicate Calculate/Retry clicks while the active request is pending. Editing remains available. An edit makes that request obsolete and allows a new calculation. A failure never clears current form values or makes an old result current. Existing previous results may be retained only with an explicit previous/outdated label; hide recommendation and contribution for the current infeasible scenario. A successful current calculation replaces prior results and clears outdated state.

Solver time_limit is 1.0 second. The browser AbortController deadline is 10 seconds, including network waiting. These are failure limits; the acceptance target remains five seconds. Use manual Retry only. No automatic retries, polling, queue or result cache is introduced. HiGHS time limits and status handling are described in \[S02\].

| **Failure or boundary**                       | **Required handling**                                                           | **Verification** |
| --------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------- |
| Invalid or excess-precision input             | Field errors; independent backend rejection; no solver call                     | T02 T04          |
| Impossible minimum orders                     | All shortages with units; no optimal recommendation; editable inputs            | T03 T04          |
| Zero production or negative contribution      | Valid optimal outcome when constraints and solver status pass                   | T03 T05          |
| Solver limit or nonoptimal status             | Safe calculation error; never show incumbent as optimal                         | T05 T13          |
| Plan fails tolerance or finite checks         | Reject entire plan; return calculation error                                    | T05              |
| Network CORS outage or browser timeout        | Preserve inputs; stop pending state; manual Retry                               | T06 T13          |
| Inputs edited during calculation              | Discard old response even if it returns successfully                            | T06              |
| Storage unavailable or quota exceeded         | No save-success claim; retain in-memory work; Retry save                        | T09              |
| Another tab changes the collection            | Reject stale mutation; reload saved collection without replacing current inputs | T10              |
| Unreadable record or unsupported schema       | Preserve raw data; warn; do not overwrite automatically                         | T09              |
| Missing outdated or incompatible saved result | Recalculate before comparison; valid inputs remain available                    | T08 T11          |
| Duplicate name or collection at capacity      | Reject new save; allow explicit rename update or delete                         | T08              |
| Delete or destructive recovery                | Confirmation naming the scenario, or explaining collection reset scope          | T08 T09          |
| Rate limit from platform                      | Safe readable limit message when possible; otherwise generic service failure    | T16              |

## Numerical checks and presentation

Recipe totals are exactly 100.00%, checked as integer basis points. For a returned plan, allow at most 0.000001 litres of production-bound or ingredient-limit deviation and at most 0.000001 minutes of processing deviation. Check all constraints using unrounded values. Keep HiGHS default numerical tolerances unless the spike identifies a reason to change them; any change must still pass the approved independent output policy \[S02\].

Display litres and minutes to three decimal places and total AUD contribution to two, using a shared Intl.NumberFormat formatter with nearest rounding and ties away from zero. Normalize displayed negative zero to zero. Accessible precision details retain the unrounded numeric representation. Charts use the same result and display formatter as tables. Compute comparison differences before display rounding; no third-party decimal package is required for display.

A shortage that rounds to zero is shown as less than 0.001 L or less than 0.001 min, with its positive value in precision details. Accepted tiny numerical residuals are disclosed as within solver tolerance rather than silently presented as exact satisfaction. Reject larger residuals before rendering. Zero-capacity utilization is No capacity; never divide by zero. Fully used resource and reached-demand labels describe constraint activity and do not promise that extra capacity improves contribution.

# 13 Performance and scalability

| **Measure**              | **Approved limit or target**                     | **Verification conditions**                                                                 |
| ------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| End-to-end calculation   | ≤5 seconds for each accepted normal calculation  | Optimize click through tables/charts rendered; includes first calculation after inactivity  |
| Concurrent demonstration | 5 simultaneous calculations each ≤5 seconds      | Three batches of five browser sessions; include actual API and rendering                    |
| Solver deadline          | 1 second                                         | Set HiGHS time_limit and test unsuccessful status handling                                  |
| Browser deadline         | 10 seconds                                       | Abort pending client request; failure deadline does not relax five-second target            |
| Request size and rate    | 16 KiB; 30 POST requests/IP/60 seconds           | Test backend byte limit and deployed WAF; pace acceptance measurements below rate limit     |
| Stored collection        | 20 entries/browser origin; names 1–50 characters | Boundary, duplicate and full-capacity update/delete tests                                   |
| Reviewer workflow        | ≤2 minutes for a first-time reviewer             | Sample calculation; save baseline; reduce orange; recalculate; save modified; compare       |
| Project cost and scale   | Free services only; no commercial SLA            | Check actual account quotas and runtime packaging during spike; record usage before release |

Use the approved sample and edited sample, representative valid boundary scenarios, and the deployed frontend/backend. Record browser/OS, connection type, location, deployment IDs, pinned versions, timestamps and each duration. Run on a stable unthrottled connection without artificial offline/throttling settings; document interruptions rather than silently excluding failures.

Collect 20 individual warm calculations, three batches of five concurrent calculations, and three first calculations after at least 30 minutes without intentionally warming the service. Also capture an initial calculation against a new deployment when possible, before health probes. An inactivity period is not proof that the host cold-started; correlate with a process-initialization marker when available and report what was observed. Backend timing alone omits browser, network and platform startup work.

Every accepted measurement must meet the target; an average cannot hide a slower first request. Pace groups across rate windows so the test does not deliberately trigger the firewall. Record rate-limit tests separately. Free-host latency remains a conditional feasibility risk. If the spike or release benchmark fails, report evidence and obtain a revised hosting/design decision before treating the target as satisfied.

The fixed three-variable model bounds computation. Expected bottlenecks are runtime initialization, SciPy import/bundle size, network delay and accidental frontend render work. Do not add workers, Redis, a database or keep-alive automation without evidence and a separate scope decision.

# 14 Observability and operations

Allen owns deployment, credentials, configuration and incident response. Emit one structured application log per calculation with server-generated request_id, outcome, error_code when applicable, and duration_ms. A process-initialization indicator may identify the first handler invocation in that process; it contains no inputs. Log safe exception categories without raw request bodies. Expose request ID in successful/error API bodies so a visitor report can be matched to current logs.

Use the Vercel runtime log and firewall/usage dashboards. Hobby runtime logs currently have one-hour retention \[S08\]; investigate promptly and retain a sanitized summary if evidence must outlive the window. No Sentry, log drain, visitor analytics, automated on-call service or server-side scenario retention is required. GitHub Actions provides test/build outcomes; use its normal owner notifications rather than adding notification integrations.

Before launch and after each release, check both project identities, deployment status, API/model versions, sample flow, allowed origins, rate-limit rule and usage. Treat a failed smoke test, incorrect output, loss/corruption caused by a write, secret exposure or repeated inability to complete the demo as a release blocker. A provider outage can require temporarily limiting calculations and showing service unavailability while local inputs remain usable.

For an incident, reproduce the failing flow, capture its request ID and deployment pair, inspect metadata logs and recent configuration changes, decide whether the issue is UI/API/storage/provider related, and use Section 17 when a recent change is responsible. Do not log private scenario values merely to diagnose a deployment. Document the fix, rerun the affected acceptance test and remove temporary debug logging before release.

# 15 Testing and verification

Use pytest for model/API tests, Vitest with React Testing Library for pure/frontend behaviour, and Playwright for real workflow tests. Run backend and frontend locally together for deterministic CI integration tests; separately verify public previews/production for hosting, CORS, firewall and latency. Mocks are appropriate for forced failures but cannot establish deployed service behaviour.

| **Test**                       | **Coverage and expected evidence**                                                                                                                                                                 |
| ------------------------------ | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| T01 Sample fixture             | Fixture values match Section 20; sample opens without saving or clearing existing records.                                                                                                         |
| T02 Input validation           | Exact 100.00% totals; excluded ingredients zero; all numeric bounds/precision; empty/nonfinite/boolean/exponent/unknown fields; min ≤ max; frontend and backend agree.                             |
| T03 Model correctness          | Baseline and orange-reduced expected plans; independent objective/usage recomputation; exact shortages in all four resources; zero capacity/time, negative profit and minimum-bound cases.         |
| T04 API contract               | 200 optimal/infeasible shapes; 400/413/415/422/409; exact fixed IDs; every field error; no solver call on invalid input; request-size streaming limit.                                             |
| T05 Solver and plan checks     | Only status 0 accepted; limit/unbounded/numerical statuses rejected; NaN/Infinity rejected; residuals just within and beyond both tolerances; alternative optima judged by objective/feasibility.  |
| T06 Freshness and timeout      | Edit during delayed response, edit then change back, load during request, duplicate clicks, manual retry, ten-second abort; old response cannot change current result.                             |
| T07 Core workflow              | Open sample calculate review; modify inputs; render tables/charts; show assumptions and zero/negative contribution; preserve inputs on failures.                                                   |
| T08 Saved management           | Save valid draft/optimal/infeasible; reopen after reload; explicit update/rename/delete; name trim/case uniqueness/length; 20th versus 21st entry; full-capacity update/delete; no autosave.       |
| T09 Recovery and versions      | Storage unavailable/quota/serialization errors; mixed valid/invalid records; unparsable envelope; unsupported schema/model; preserved bytes; explicit reset/removal; unsaved state remains usable. |
| T10 Concurrency                | Two tabs both attempt mutation; exclusive lock and revision reject stale write; storage event; reload collection preserves unsaved form; unsupported lock capability produces safe save failure.   |
| T11 Comparison                 | Two distinct saved current optimal results; block drafts/infeasible/outdated/model mismatch; compare inputs/results and B−A deltas from unrounded values.                                          |
| T12 Accessibility and browsers | Chromium Firefox WebKit at 360/768/1280 widths; keyboard/focus/errors/status/contrast/zoom/reflow/table alternatives; record available real-device checks separately.                              |
| T13 Calculation failures       | Forced solver limit/failure; network/offline/invalid response/CORS/provider failure; correct message, no optimal label, manual retry and input preservation.                                       |
| T14 Deployed performance       | Approved 20 individual, three five-session batches, and three after-inactivity runs; browser timings and deployment evidence, not API averages only.                                               |
| T15 Reviewer usability         | Time a first-time reviewer through the documented sample/save/edit/save/compare flow; all steps ≤2 minutes. A self-rehearsal is preparation, not first-time-user evidence.                         |
| T16 Security and privacy       | Deployed rate rule, exact CORS origins, byte/schema limits, public preview, no client secret, safe name rendering, redacted logs and repository secret/dependency review.                          |
| T17 Release smoke              | Public frontend and backend; sample/edited save compare; reload; API/model identity; old frontend remains compatible during backend-first release.                                                 |
| T18 Rollback rehearsal         | Restore prior deployment/configuration pair; current browser collection preserved; re-run core flow; record manual restore steps and platform limitations.                                         |

## Model fixtures beyond the sample

Use a zero-demand fixture with all min=max=0, which must return zero quantities and zero contribution. Use strictly negative contribution with zero minima, which must also produce zero. A feasible positive minimum with negative contribution remains valid and may produce negative total contribution. All-zero processing coefficients must work without dividing by zero; finite demand caps still bound production.

For shortage coverage, retain sample recipes but set every minimum and maximum to 10 L, orange/apple/pineapple availability to 1 L each, and processing capacity to zero. Exact required resources are orange 9 L, apple 12 L, pineapple 9 L and processing 70 min. All four shortages must be returned. Test tiny positive decimal shortages separately so display cannot hide them.

Validate baseline optimality independently: positive optimal quantities are 50, 20 and 100/3 L; the resource multipliers 11/24 for orange, 3/4 for apple, zero for pineapple and 57/80 for processing satisfy all three profit equations. Capacity-weighted multipliers yield the same 658/3 AUD objective. Use this as a known-solution certificate rather than comparing only one solver run against another.

Accessibility verification combines automated checks with keyboard, focus, screen-reader status/field associations, dark-theme contrast and zoom inspection against applicable WCAG 2.2 AA criteria \[S14\]. Equivalent tables are required for both charts. Playwright WebKit is engine coverage, not a claim that real iOS Safari was tested. Record actual devices available during implementation and any unverified device coverage honestly.

# 16 Deployment and rollout

## Environment setup and paired previews

1. Create a personal public repository, add both folders, and run local checks. Provision two free Vercel Hobby projects with root directories frontend and backend. Confirm free-plan usage and dependency bundle limits in the actual account before relying on them.
2. Set framework/runtime detection and the supported backend entrypoint app/main.py exporting app. Pin the selected compatible dependencies. Verify Python 3.12 and Node.js 24 settings. Use local uvicorn app.main:app for development; do not package development test tools into production requirements.
3. Disable automatic Git deployments for both projects using git.deploymentEnabled=false, and verify a push does not publish production \[S15\]. GitHub Actions still runs tests and builds automatically. Create previews and releases manually through the linked project folders, so a passing test does not itself publish a release.
4. Assign two available, preview-specific .vercel.app aliases, one for each project, using the Vercel CLI alias command \[S21\]. Verify the aliases during the initial spike and keep them distinct from production domains. Set the frontend preview API base URL to the stable backend preview alias, and the backend preview ALLOWED_ORIGINS to the stable frontend preview origin. Reassign the same aliases after new preview deployments, so unique deployment URLs do not create a circular configuration change. Never solve pairing by allowing all Vercel domains or buying a domain.
5. Confirm public preview accessibility and both preflight and actual POST requests. A protected preview can block cross-origin requests before FastAPI sees them \[S09\]. Do not put protection-bypass secrets in browser code. Apply input/rate safeguards to the public preview API.
6. Run the full paired smoke flow, deployed error checks and performance evidence. Preview and production browser collections are separate. Record the final URLs/configurations used, not placeholder URLs.

## CI and release gates

| **Gate**                            | **Required evidence**                                                                                                                                                  |
| ----------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| G01 Hosting feasibility             | Ten-hour spike: deployable solver bundle; correct sample/shortages; paired CORS; latency evidence including first-after-inactivity. Failure returns to owner decision. |
| G02 Correctness and contract        | Frontend type/lint/build checks; backend tests; validation/model/contract/freshness tests pass against pinned versions.                                                |
| G03 Complete product workflow       | FR01–FR14 acceptance tests pass, including save/reopen/manage/compare and recovery.                                                                                    |
| G04 Public safeguards and usability | 16 KiB/30-per-minute controls, redacted logs, no exposed secrets, accessibility/browser matrix and first-time ≤2-minute walkthrough evidence.                          |
| G05 Performance and recovery        | T14 each measurement passes; deployment/configuration records exist; rollback rehearsal passes; free-plan limits remain appropriate.                                   |
| G06 Production verification         | Manual backend-first then frontend release; public smoke passes; public repository and README available.                                                               |

GitHub Actions runs frontend lint/type/build and unit/component tests, backend pytest, contract fixtures, and Playwright against locally started services. Use a reproducible dependency install with the committed lockfile/requirements. Browser installs must match the pinned Playwright version \[S11\]. Keep live-host latency tests manual or explicitly owner-triggered and paced; do not turn CI into repeated free-host load or keep-alive traffic.

## Manual production release

1. Record the candidate commit, passing CI run, paired-preview results, previous production deployment IDs and previous effective environment/firewall settings. Confirm the backend is compatible with the currently live frontend and saved schema before proceeding.
2. Set backend production ALLOWED_ORIGINS to the stable frontend production origin. From the correctly linked backend folder, run the manual production deployment, for example vercel --prod \[S16\]. Verify service identity and the currently live frontend calculation before releasing the frontend.
3. Set frontend production NEXT_PUBLIC_BACKEND_URL to the stable backend production base URL. Deploy the correctly linked frontend project manually. Production environment values must be set before building; do not promote a preview build with preview API configuration as though it were a production build.
4. Verify the complete sample/edit/save/compare/reload flow, input errors and public access. Inspect metadata logs and usage while running those checks. Record both deployment IDs, effective origins and model/schema versions in the release record. Use Section 17 if verification fails.

There is no database migration, feature flag platform, rolling release or commercial traffic split for this MVP. Browser schema version stays at 1. Future incompatible API/model/schema changes must preserve old inputs and pass mixed-version and rollback checks before release. The manual sequence is necessary because the two projects do not release atomically.

# 17 Rollback runbook

Allen initiates rollback when a release causes incorrect calculations, stale results presented as current, broken public calls, unsafe saved-data writes, or a failed required smoke flow. A provider outage without a recent app/config change requires provider diagnosis rather than an assumed rollback fix. On Hobby, Instant Rollback is limited to the immediately previous production deployment; check that both rollback targets are still retained \[S17\].

| **Step**                | **Action and verification**                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| ----------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| 1 Contain               | Stop further releases. Record current/previous deployment pair and the failure/request ID. If calculations are unsafe, temporarily block the optimize route through the firewall and keep a clear frontend failure message.                        |
| 2 Check compatibility   | Confirm the previous frontend can read schema 1 and work with the current backend. If newer unsupported browser data exists, preserve it without downgrade/reset; choose a compatible forward fix if rollback would be destructive.                |
| 3 Restore frontend      | Use the frontend project's prior production deployment through dashboard Instant Rollback or CLI rollback. Confirm its embedded API base URL points to the intended backend. Do not assume current environment settings rebuild an old deployment. |
| 4 Restore backend       | If the backend change caused the issue and compatibility permits, restore its prior production deployment. Restore the effective origin/settings record when a new rebuild is needed; check health identity and actual frontend POST.              |
| 5 Restore configuration | Compare deployment protection, firewall rule and allowed origins with the saved baseline. Revert relevant control-plane changes explicitly; they are not guaranteed to roll back with application code.                                            |
| 6 Preserve browser data | No server database restore is needed. Never clear localStorage automatically. Verify the existing collection can reopen and compare, or remains preserved with a compatibility warning.                                                            |
| 7 Verify recovery       | Run sample and edited model, save/reopen/compare and failure preservation tests against the public pair. Inspect current logs. Remove any temporary route block only after correct results are confirmed.                                          |
| 8 Repair and record     | Document incident cause and effective restored pair. If the previous deployment is unavailable, rebuild the recorded commit with its recorded production configuration and checks. Rehearse again before releasing the fix.                        |

Rolling back a build does not update its compiled frontend environment values, restore independent firewall changes or reverse browser records \[S17\]. A service-URL change requires rebuilding the frontend with the correct production URL. No claim is made that free-host recovery has a guaranteed elapsed-time SLA.

# 18 Implementation plan

The approved allocation is 180 hours across 12 relative weeks. Calendar dates remain unassigned. Track actual hours, spike outcomes and acceptance evidence. No learning timebox or investigation is added on top of this budget.

| **Weeks** | **Hours** | **Work and dependency**                                                                                                                         |
| --------- | --------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| 1         | 15        | Hosting/Python API investigation capped at 10 hours; remaining time for API foundations and setup. G01 must pass before committing to the host. |
| 2–3       | 30        | Trusted validation, exact shortages, LP construction, solver output checks and API contracts. Requires viable deployment path.                  |
| 4–6       | 45        | Dark dashboard, form states, results, charts, assumptions and responsive interface. Uses stable contract fixtures and real API.                 |
| 7–8       | 30        | Saved drafts/results, naming/capacity, version recovery, locked writes, comparison and delete confirmation.                                     |
| 9–10      | 30        | Full automation, accessibility/browser checks, failure tests and deployed performance/usability evidence.                                       |
| 11        | 15        | Public release, README, release/configuration record and rollback rehearsal.                                                                    |
| 12        | 15        | Contingency, acceptance fixes and honest portfolio evidence. Do not use this reserve to add excluded features.                                  |
| Total     | 180       | All hours include learning, verification, deployment and documentation.                                                                         |

## Week one investigation

Question: can a free Vercel Python service package the selected SciPy stack and meet the approved click-to-render target? Output: pinned dependencies, a deployed calculation/shortage response, paired frontend/backend CORS evidence, actual bundle/runtime settings, and measured warm/concurrent/after-inactivity behaviour. Use a minimal frontend harness until the dashboard exists. The harness demonstrates integration feasibility; final performance and the reviewer flow must be retested on the completed dashboard.

Success requires correct sample results, safe input/error behaviour, a deployable free-tier bundle and evidence meeting the approved timing scope. If the ten-hour cap is reached without proof, record the failing dimension, remaining options and likely budget impact. Allen must approve a hosting/design change before dependent work continues. Do not replace the public backend with a local script or relax first-request timing without approval.

## Definition of done and portfolio evidence

Done means all P0 product requirements and approved technical checks pass, frontend/backend are public, and the repository explains reproducible setup, the model, units, assumptions, limitations, test commands, result freshness, local saving and deployment. Include benchmark and rollback records plus screenshots or a short reviewer walkthrough. Resume claims must reflect completed evidence; API deployment experience is earned through this project, not assumed in the starting profile.

# 19 Risks and decisions

| **Risk**                                  | **Impact and response**                                                                                                                                        | **Status**                      |
| ----------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------- |
| Free-host startup or SciPy packaging      | Could prevent five-second completion. Week-one capped spike and final T14 gate; owner decision if unmet.                                                       | Open feasibility risk           |
| New Python API workflow                   | Could consume more time than scripts/coursework. Separate schema/model/API modules and early deployed proof.                                                   | Approved learning scope         |
| Two projects and public previews          | CORS/configuration mismatches or partial releases. Exact pairing, production-specific builds and backend-first compatibility checks.                           | Mitigated by design             |
| Local data loss or corruption             | Browser clearing/origin change can remove access. Explicit local-scope notice; preserve corrupt/unsupported records; no cloud backup promise.                  | Accepted product limit          |
| Floating-point or stale result errors     | Could recommend an invalid/current-looking plan. Exact entered-decimal checks, output tolerances, independent tests and revision guards.                       | Required verification           |
| Public endpoint abuse or quota exhaustion | IP rule is regional and not identity-based. Body/schema/solver limits; free usage checks; temporary restriction when needed.                                   | Accepted bounded demo risk      |
| Rollback incompatibility                  | Independent configuration or future schema changes may survive rollback. Record effective configuration and preserve browser data; forward fix when necessary. | Required rehearsal              |
| Unverified real-device coverage           | Engine emulation is not actual device testing. Record devices and coverage limitations during acceptance.                                                      | Implementation evidence pending |
| Reviewer timing and scope creep           | First-time flow may exceed two minutes; extra features consume reserve. Test concise instructions and maintain fixed P0 scope.                                 | Required acceptance             |

## Architecture decision summary

| **Decision**           | **Approved choice and rationale**                                                                                             |
| ---------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| ADR01 Runtime boundary | Next.js frontend plus separate FastAPI backend; Python API learning and optimizer execution remain explicit.                  |
| ADR02 Solver           | SciPy linprog method highs; continuous decisions and finite bounds; no licensed external solver service.                      |
| ADR03 Storage          | Versioned localStorage collection; explicit saves, no accounts/database; lock and revision protect multiple tabs.             |
| ADR04 Hosting          | Two Vercel Hobby projects are the first candidate, conditional on the ten-hour feasibility investigation; free services only. |
| ADR05 Numeric policy   | Exact decimal input/recipe validation; litre/minute output tolerance 0.000001; separate display precision.                    |
| ADR06 Failure policy   | One-second solver limit, ten-second browser deadline, manual Retry, preserve inputs and discard stale responses.              |
| ADR07 Delivery         | Automatic CI; public paired previews; manual production releases and recorded rollback pair.                                  |
| ADR08 Verification     | Three engines/widths; five simultaneous calculations; approved sample, after-inactivity and first-time reviewer evidence.     |

No unresolved product or architecture preference blocks the initial spike. Hosting feasibility, real-device availability, exact package pins, repository URL and calendar start date are implementation facts still to record. These must not be represented as already verified. A change to scope, cost, timing targets or architecture requires a new decision; routine module details follow this approved specification.

# 20 Appendices

## Model definition

For each blend, the decision is litres produced that day. Ingredient coefficients are recipe percentages divided by 100; processing coefficients are minutes per litre. The objective maximizes total contribution. Each quantity lies between its entered minimum and maximum. The three ingredient constraints and shared processing constraint must stay within capacity.

Figure 4 Continuous daily production model

For SciPy, use c as the negative of the contribution vector, A_ub as the three recipe rows plus the processing row, b_ub as ingredient litres plus capacity minutes, and bounds as each minimum/maximum pair. Keep continuous decisions and default presolve; accept only successful optimal status \[S01, S02\].

## Approved fictional fixture

| **Blend**       | **Orange %** | **Apple %** | **Pineapple %** | **AUD per L** | **Minutes per L** | **Min to max L** |
| --------------- | ------------ | ----------- | --------------- | ------------- | ----------------- | ---------------- |
| Orange–apple    | 60           | 40          | 0               | 2.00          | 2                 | 0–60             |
| Apple–pineapple | 0            | 50          | 50              | 1.80          | 2                 | 0–60             |
| Tropical        | 30           | 30          | 40              | 2.50          | 3                 | 0–60             |

Initial capacities: orange 40 L, apple 40 L, pineapple 30 L and four processing hours, equivalent to 240 minutes. The comparison fixture changes only orange availability to 30 L. These are synthetic teaching/demo values, not a real producer's costs or recipes.

| **Output**          | **Baseline** | **Orange reduced** | **B minus A** |
| ------------------- | ------------ | ------------------ | ------------- |
| Orange–apple L      | 50.000       | 25.000             | −25.000       |
| Apple–pineapple L   | 20.000       | 20.000             | 0.000         |
| Tropical L          | 33.333       | 50.000             | 16.667        |
| Contribution AUD    | 219.33       | 211.00             | −8.33         |
| Orange used L       | 40.000       | 30.000             | −10.000       |
| Apple used L        | 40.000       | 35.000             | −5.000        |
| Pineapple used L    | 23.333       | 30.000             | 6.667         |
| Processing used min | 240.000      | 240.000            | 0.000         |

Unrounded baseline tropical production is 100/3 L and baseline contribution is 658/3 AUD. Floating-point output may differ in its last digits within the approved policy. All sample calculations were checked locally during planning; hosted timings have not been measured.

## Glossary

| **Term**                         | **Meaning**                                                                                                 |
| -------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Profit contribution              | Sales contribution after the entered variable cost assumptions; not guaranteed overall business profit.     |
| Continuous decision              | Fractional litres are allowed; integer bottle counts are excluded.                                          |
| Binding or fully used            | A constraint is reached within the defined tolerance. This does not establish a benefit from increasing it. |
| CORS                             | Browser permission for cross-origin requests; distinct from authentication.                                 |
| ASGI                             | Python web application interface used by FastAPI and the host.                                              |
| Canonical snapshot               | An immutable normalized input copy used to check that a result belongs to the current inputs.               |
| Schema version and model version | Stored-format compatibility and mathematical-model compatibility are checked separately.                    |
| Spike                            | A capped investigation with a concrete question, output and success criterion.                              |
